summary: Reusable docs sidebar: an `active` prop ('getting-started'|'navigation'|'notebook'|'under-the-hood') selects which group's anchor sub-list expands — only the current page's section outline shows, other groups collapse to a single link (nextjs.org-style progressive disclosure). Each group's top-level link is rendered as `<a class="gh gh-link">`, which unintentionally matches docs.css's global `.side a.active` rule (background + left-border pill) whenever it's the active group — producing a double-highlighted box stacked on top of the active sub-link's own pill. Fixed with a local scoped override forcing `.gh-link` and `.gh-link.active` back to `background:none; border-left-color:transparent`.
incidentAliases: group header boxed like active link

summary: Reusable docs sidebar: an `active` prop ('getting-started'|'navigation'|'notebook'|'under-the-hood') selects which group expands its anchor sub-list; other groups collapse to a single link. Only the ACTIVE group's label carries the `gh` class (uppercase, tracked, muted — docs.css `.side-group .gh`). Every group used to carry it, so on any page the three inactive groups rendered as section headers with nothing beneath them: headings labelling nothing. The `.gh-link` scoped override still exists and is load-bearing for a different reason — it cancels docs.css's global `.side a.active` pill so the active group header is not double-highlighted on top of the active sub-link's own pill.
